title: Microsoft Entra: sensitivity labels for cloud security groups
summary: The briefing's rollout, tenant enablement, preview limitations and feature-specific prerequisites are supported. Minor corrections should clarify conflicting general licensing guidance, tidy the controls presentation and identify checklist controls missing from the table.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans sensitivity labels for Microsoft Entra cloud security groups.
claims.quote: Apply sensitivity labels to Microsoft Entra cloud security groups to extend the classification and governance you already use for Microsoft 365 groups.

claims.claim: Label-based protection already exists for Microsoft 365 groups and SharePoint sites.
claims.quote: This capability extends label-based protection currently available for Microsoft 365 groups and SharePoint sites to cloud security groups.

claims.claim: The same published groups-and-sites labels apply without separate label configuration.
claims.quote: The same labels you publish in the Microsoft Purview portal and configure for groups and sites apply automatically to cloud security groups, with no separate label configuration required.

claims.claim: Labels enforce membership and guest access policies when groups are created or labelled.
claims.quote: automatically enforce membership and guest access policies when groups are created or labeled.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development"

claims.quote: Published 2026-10-14; last updated 2026-11-14; Microsoft's end date 2027-02-26

claims.claim: The notice schedules rollout to begin in mid-January 2027.

claims.claim: The notice names the Entra admin center, Azure portal, PowerShell and Microsoft Graph as assignment surfaces.
claims.quote: Labels can be assigned through the Microsoft Entra admin center, Azure portal, PowerShell, or Microsoft Graph.

claims.claim: Administrators can assign labels during creation or after a group has been created.
claims.quote: Administrators will be able to apply published Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels to cloud security groups during group creation or after a group has been created.

claims.claim: No action is required to receive the change, although use requires tenant enablement.
claims.quote:
No action is required to receive this change.

- To use sensitivity labels with Microsoft Entra security groups after rollout:

claims.claim: The notice promises support for changing assigned labels in a future update without giving its date.
claims.quote: Support for changing assigned labels will be introduced in a future update.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The control is admin-opt-in: cloud security group labelling requires administrator enablement.
claims.quote: To apply sensitivity labels to cloud security groups, you must enable the feature by creating or updating tenant-level directory settings.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[0].note; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: Cloud security groups use Group.Security separately from the Group.Unified setting for Microsoft 365 groups.
claims.quote: Cloud security groups use the `Group.Security` settings template, which is separate from the `Group.Unified` template used for Microsoft 365 groups.

claims.claim: Learn describes the feature as preview despite the roadmap's future GA target.
claims.quote: This feature is in preview.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; controls[1].note; Governance guidance
claims.claim: During preview, a label cannot be changed or removed after assignment.
claims.quote: Label immutability: You can't change or remove a label after you apply it. Choose labels carefully before you apply them.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn says label mutability and enforcement for high-privilege roles might change before GA.
claims.quote: Certain behaviors, including the ability to change labels once they're set and enforcement for high-privilege roles, might change before general availability.

claims.claim: Security groups are authorisation primitives used in Conditional Access scoping, application access and resource permissions.
claims.quote: Security groups are used directly in authorization decisions such as Conditional Access scoping, application access, and resource permissions.

claims.claim: Enforcement depends on Microsoft Entra ID membership resolution and validation.
claims.quote: Enforcement depends on Microsoft Entra ID's membership resolution and validation logic, not on administrative governance practices alone.

claims.claim: Learn states that current validation processes apply only at creation or first label assignment.
claims.quote: Current validation processes apply only on group creation or when a label is first assigned.

claims.claim: Learn says extension of those validation processes is in progress.
claims.quote: Extending these validation processes for other scenarios is in progress.

claims.claim: Purview label policy changes do not alter existing group membership.
claims.quote: Sensitivity label policy changes in Microsoft Purview apply immediately to new policy checks, but they don't alter existing group membership.

claims.claim: Guests already in a group remain after its label policy changes to block guests until an owner or admin removes them.
claims.quote: guests already in those groups remain until an owner or admin removes them.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises against changing or deleting a label's policy once used on security groups.
claims.quote: Avoid changing or deleting a label's policy after the label is in use on security groups.

claims.claim: During preview, listed admin roles including Global Administrator, User Administrator and Groups Administrator can bypass enforcement when adding members.
claims.quote:
The following admin roles and application permissions can bypass label policy enforcement when adding members. This behavior might change before general availability.

    - Admin roles: Global Administrator, User Administrator, Groups Administrator

claims.claim: Apps with Group.ReadWrite.All, Directory.ReadWrite.All, Directory.ReadWriteAdvanced.All or GroupMember.ReadWrite.All can bypass label enforcement during preview.
claims.quote: Application permissions: `Group.ReadWrite.All`, `Directory.ReadWrite.All`, `Directory.ReadWriteAdvanced.All`, `GroupMember.ReadWrite.All`

claims.claim: Dynamic-membership security groups are unsupported, including edge cases where a label can be applied without policy enforcement.
claims.quote: You can't apply sensitivity labels to security groups with dynamic membership in this release. While there are certain edge cases where you can apply a label to a dynamic group, the associated label policy isn't enforced.

claims.claim: Security groups synchronised from on-premises Active Directory are unsupported.
claims.quote: Security groups synced from on-premises Active Directory and Exchange-managed security groups aren't supported.

claims.claim: Exchange-managed security groups are unsupported.
claims.quote: Security groups synced from on-premises Active Directory and Exchange-managed security groups aren't supported.

claims.claim: Mail-enabled security groups are unsupported.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labels for mail-enabled security groups and distribution lists aren't supported.

claims.claim: Distribution lists are unsupported.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labels for mail-enabled security groups and distribution lists aren't supported.

claims.claim: The described capability applies labels and enforces membership policy rather than adding autonomous actions.
claims.quote: organizations can apply published Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels directly to security groups and automatically enforce membership and guest access policies when groups are created or labeled.

claims.claim: The documented workaround for a wrong label is a new security group with the correct label and re-added members.
claims.quote: To change a label, create a new security group with the correct label, and then re-add the members to the new group.

claims.where: Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Nested groups must be removed before labelling a parent group.
claims.quote: You can't label a group that currently contains nested groups. To label a parent group, remove all nested (child) groups first, apply the label to the parent, and then add the child groups back.

claims.claim: Child groups must have labels at least as restrictive as the parent's.
claims.quote: When you add a child group back to a labeled parent, the child group's label must be at least as restrictive as the parent's label.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 admin center does not support assigning sensitivity labels to security groups.
claims.quote: Assigning sensitivity labels to security groups isn't supported in the Microsoft 365 admin center or in the My Groups portal.

claims.claim: The My Groups portal does not support assigning sensitivity labels to security groups.
claims.quote: Assigning sensitivity labels to security groups isn't supported in the Microsoft 365 admin center or in the My Groups portal.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The feature page requires at least one active Entra ID P1 or P2 licence, or Microsoft 365 E3/E5, in the organisation.
claims.quote: Your organization has at least one active Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 license (or Microsoft 365 E3/E5).

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Licensing is included in eligible existing subscriptions.
claims.quote:
Sensitivity labeling, including automatic or policy-based labeling, requires a Microsoft 365 E5 license or Microsoft 365 Information Protection and Governance (IPG).
| Manual Sensitivity Labeling | Included | Included | Included | Included | Included |
claims.fix: Retain included and the feature page's prerequisites. Add this service-description URL to sources and add: 'The service description lists manual sensitivity labelling as included in Microsoft 365 E3/E5, but also contains a broader statement that sensitivity labelling requires Microsoft 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 Information Protection and Governance (IPG); the feature page specifically lists Entra ID P1/P2 or Microsoft 365 E3/E5.'

claims.claim: The notice cites Microsoft 365 E3 or E5 as eligible licensing that includes Entra ID P1.
claims.quote: Confirm that your organization has eligible licensing, such as Microsoft 365 E3 or Microsoft 365 E5, which includes Microsoft Entra ID P1.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate feature price or meter is published in the examined Microsoft documentation as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "cloud security groups" "sensitivity labels" licensing pricing meter. Opened learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/users/groups-sensitivity-labels and the Microsoft Purview service description, sensitivity-labeling section; neither specifies a separate feature price or meter.

claims.claim: The assigning user must be a group owner or at least a Groups Administrator.
claims.quote: The current signed-in user has sufficient privileges to assign sensitivity labels (group owner or at least a Groups Administrator)

claims.claim: The assigning user must be within the label publishing policy's scope.
claims.quote: and is within the scope of the sensitivity label publishing policy.

claims.claim: Labels must be published in Purview with the Groups & Sites scope enabled.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labels are published in the Microsoft Purview portal with the Groups & Sites scope enabled.

claims.claim: Execute-AzureADLabelSync synchronisation is a prerequisite for using the labels in Entra ID.
claims.quote: Labels are synchronized to Microsoft Entra ID by using the `Execute-AzureADLabelSync` cmdlet.

claims.claim: Labels can take up to 24 hours after synchronisation to become available.
claims.quote: Labels can take up to 24 hours after synchronization to become available.

claims.claim: Execute-AzureADLabelSync runs only in Security & Compliance PowerShell, not the Graph SDK.
claims.quote: The `Execute-AzureADLabelSync` cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell, not in the Microsoft Graph PowerShell SDK.

claims.claim: No admin-centre toggle is documented for enabling cloud security group sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: Searched: "cloud security groups" "EnableMIPLabels" "admin center" enable. Opened learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/users/groups-sensitivity-labels; enablement is documented through directory settings in PowerShell, not an admin-centre toggle.

claims.claim: New-MgBetaDirectorySetting -BodyParameter $params enables labels with the specified Group.Security template and EnableMIPLabels=True.
claims.quote:
templateId = "d209f6fa-3839-4d70-b83f-60b1c64d0e8f"
                name = "EnableMIPLabels"
                value = "True"
    New-MgBetaDirectorySetting -BodyParameter $params

claims.claim: Existing Group.Security settings are changed using Update-MgBetaDirectorySetting.
claims.quote:
If the settings already exist and you need to update them:
Update-MgBetaDirectorySetting -DirectorySettingId $Setting.Id `
    -BodyParameter $params

claims.claim: Existing group labels are assigned in Entra admin center > Microsoft Entra ID > Groups > All groups > group > Properties > Sensitivity label.
claims.quote:
Select Microsoft Entra ID.
Select Groups > All groups, and then select the group you want to label.
On the group's page, select Properties.
Select a sensitivity label from the Sensitivity label dropdown.

claims.claim: PATCH /v1.0/groups/{id} sets assignedLabels to assign the group's label.
claims.quote: The list of sensitivity label pairs (label ID, label name) associated with a Microsoft 365 group or a cloud security group. Requires a Microsoft Entra ID P1 license. This property can be specified during group creation or update. However, for cloud security groups, it's immutable once set.
claims.fix: Set controls[1].api.call to 'PATCH /v1.0/groups/{id}' and add to its note: 'The request body sets the assignedLabels collection with the label ID.' Make the same presentation change in the rendered table.

claims.claim: Graph requires delegated Group.ManageProtection.All for cloud security group assignedLabels; app-only is unsupported.
claims.quote: Group.ManageProtection.All delegated permission is the least privileged permission to update the assignedLabels property for cloud security groups. App-only scenarios aren't supported.

claims.claim: The new-group entry point is Groups > All groups > New group in the same Entra navigation.
claims.quote:
Select Microsoft Entra ID.
Select Groups > All groups > New group.

claims.claim: No UI operation is documented for explicitly synchronising published labels into Entra ID.
claims.quote: Searched: "cloud security groups" sensitivity labels synchronize portal change remove audit. Opened the feature page and Execute-AzureADLabelSync reference; search also returned Purview's container synchronisation instructions, which specify PowerShell, not a UI sync operation.

claims.claim: Execute-AzureADLabelSync starts sensitivity label synchronisation into Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: Use the Execute-AzureADLabelSync cmdlet to start the synchronization of sensitivity labels into Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.claim: The label-management route is Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels
claims.fix: For the existing-label editing route, extend controls[3].ui.path to 'Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > label > Edit label'. Its note may continue to explain selecting the Groups & Sites scope. Update the rendered table to match.

claims.claim: Set-Label -Identity <label> -SiteAndGroupProtectionEnabled <$true|$false> enables or disables the label's Site and Group Protection action.
claims.quote:
The SiteAndGroupProtectionEnabled parameter enables or disables the Site and Group Protection action for the label. Valid values are:
- $true: The Site and Group Protection action is enabled.
- $false: The Site and Group Protection action is disabled.

claims.claim: The general Purview Set-Label control is presented as not confirmed for cloud security groups.
claims.quote: You can now use Security & Compliance PowerShell to create and configure all the settings you see in your labeling admin center.
claims.fix: Replace the uncertainty in controls[3].note and the final Governance controls paragraph with: 'General Purview control: Set-Label modifies the published label; SiteAndGroupProtectionEnabled enables or disables its Site and Group Protection action. Cloud security groups use the same labels configured for groups and sites.'

claims.claim: Neither UI nor API supports changing or removing an assigned cloud security group label during preview.
claims.quote: During preview, you can't change sensitivity labels on cloud security groups. After you apply a label, you can't modify or remove it.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; After rollout
claims.claim: The checklist asks readers to inventory group membership and remove existing guests, but the table has no membership-management control.
claims.quote: Inventory security groups that contain guests, nested groups, dynamic membership or on-premises sync ... Check labelled groups for guests ... and remove them where the policy requires.
claims.fix: The inventory step and the existing-guest removal step have no matching membership-management row. Remove those two checklist bullets rather than adding an unverified control row.

claims.claim: Guest membership can conflict with assigning a label that blocks guest access.
claims.quote: Applying a label that blocks guest access to a group that contains guest members. Resolution: Remove the guest members, then apply the label.

claims.claim: Documentation of audit events specifically for label assignment on security groups remains an open question.
claims.quote: Searched: "security groups" "sensitivity label" "audit" assignment Entra. Read the feature page and the Audit log activities search excerpt: the latter explicitly describes Microsoft 365 Groups auditing, not cloud security group label assignment events.
